LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Stage_Range: Learn how soft docking works. Explore the optional weapons range, or head to the station and return later.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Tutorial_Dialog_Range:
Takeoff, matching velocity and exterior work: you have learned the essentials. Congratulations!

There is also soft docking. Enable the docking indicators at the lower right of your PDA. Face two ports toward each other and overlap their outer diamonds; keep them aligned until the connection completes. Stop manual flight and use Organize transfer at the port to send people across.

Before collecting your new ship, I recommend visiting the weapons range southeast of the wreck. The western structure is the platform; the eastern one is its target. Follow the gold arrow and operate the entrance terminal; acknowledging its instructions unlocks the blast door.

Starbound developed kinetic and electromagnetic line shields for local combat. They have very different strengths and weaknesses from traditional guard domes. You may not have encountered them before your voyage. Experimenting here could save your life in a pirate fight.

Nothing here is an exam. Look around as long as you like, then reopen this guidance to arrange the handover. You can also collect the new ship first and visit the range later.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Unshielded:
All three target shields are off. Fire matching cannon types from the northern main and southern secondary rows at the six layers of steel. Compare the shape of the breach, the area damaged and the depth. Use intact armour for each shot where possible.

CHEMICAL GUNS
Propellant drives the shot out of the barrel. Increasing the charge at the same head mass raises muzzle velocity and generally generates more heat. At a fixed charge, a heavier round leaves the muzzle more slowly with the same muzzle-frame kinetic energy. Penetration depends on the energy of the shot relative to the point it hits on the target.
An intact high-explosive steel shell detonates on structure contact. Heavier shells make stronger, wider blasts, and damage falls off with distance from the centre. Main-set rapid fire clears exposed equipment over an area. The main heavy cannon can open a wide breach. Secondary-set uranium penetrates successive layers along the shot path. Its rapid cannon handles exposed equipment and thin armour, and its heavy cannon can cut a narrow, deep channel. Matching guns use the same charge and head count, with uranium giving the heavier shot. Relative target motion also affects the impact.

LASERS AND RAILGUN
At power 3 a laser pulse deals 48 structural damage in the cell it hits. Lasers draw stored power and are useful for precise attacks on exposed equipment.
The ten-cell secondary group 4 railgun uses a loader and nine accelerators. Each shot uses 45 uranium heads. A fully powered shot costs 6,750 Wd and, head-on against a stationary target, can pierce six steel layers or put about 5,000 points of demand on guard capacity. Heavy-cannon salvos cost less energy, are harder to land repeatedly in the same place and generally break guard shields more slowly. Railguns excel at opening a fight and penetrating deep armour, but oblique kinetic shields can destabilize their rods.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Kinetic:
The target kinetic shield is set to {0} degrees at {1}% strength. The four settings are 0 degrees at 35%, and 45 degrees at 7%, 35% and 100%. Keep the same gun firing due east and compare the two 35% settings to see what changing the incidence angle does.

IMPULSE AND PROJECTILES
The shield applies impulse along its normal and preserves tangential velocity. With enough power, 7%, 35% and 100% deliver 25.2, 126 and 360 impulse, respectively. The same impulse changes a heavier round's velocity less. Near normal incidence the shot mainly slows, although a strong pulse can send a light round back. A sideways impulse can tumble an entire round or tear it into fragments. Ordinary rounds tear into three pieces, and rail rods can split into four. Tumbling steel deals kinetic contact damage only. Intact uranium still penetrates according to its remaining impact energy.
All five solid rounds stay intact at 0 degrees and 35%. At 45 degrees and 7%, rapid steel and the rail rod start tumbling. At 35%, rapid uranium and heavy steel start tumbling. At 100%, heavy uranium also tumbles. Previously destabilized rounds can break further. Actual incidence depends on the shot and shield normal. Aim, spread and the motion of either ship affect it.

POWER AND COUNTERS
The shield needs power to maintain its field. A hit costs a processing fee, an impulse charge and any positive work done on the projectile. If energy runs short, the shield pays for the impulse it can afford and briefly drops out. Rapid hits can drain the battery bank. The platform's guard shield catches returns, so keep other ships out of the firing lane. Lasers, missiles and boarding craft pass through kinetic line shields.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_KineticComparison: 35% HEAVY CANNON COMPARISON\nWith a powered shield and intact armour, fire the main group 2 steel heavy cannon once due east. Then enable secondary group 2 and fire the uranium heavy cannon once due east. The steel round tumbles and deals only kinetic impact damage when it hits. The uranium round stays intact and continues through the armour. Compare how many layers each shot crosses. To isolate incidence, fire the same heavy cannon at 0 degrees and 35% as well.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Electromagnetic:
The target electromagnetic shield is set to {0} degrees at {1}% strength. Fire one group 3 laser due east and watch the beam segments on either side of the shield. From north to south the four settings are 0 degrees at 20%, then 45 degrees at 20%, 50% and 100%. Compare incidence at 20%, then compare the three 45-degree strengths. Left mouse defaults to main group 3 and right mouse to secondary group 3 when enabled.

The shield first refracts the beam passively. A head-on beam carries straight on, an oblique beam bends and an angle above the critical value can give passive reflection. At 0% the field still requires power and still bends light. Active strength turns the outgoing beam further toward its incoming path. The additional turn can reach 36 degrees at 20% and 90 degrees at 50%. Fire due east at the 45-degree shield. With full power, at 20% the beam bends and still travels east. At 50% it turns back toward the front of the shield. At 100% it returns along the incoming path. The active cost follows beam power and the actual added turn. A power shortfall weakens the turn and briefly disables the line.
Both range lasers use power 3 and 6 Wd per pulse. Reflecting the full power-3 medium beam at normal incidence costs the shield about 1.2 Wd per pulse. A redirected beam can still hit another surface. The platform guard can catch returns. Try a solid round from a cannon or the railgun to see it pass through. Missiles and boarding craft also pass through.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_GuardSingle:
Only the primary guard shield is enabled. Guard spends capacity to absorb incoming rounds and beams. Weapons inside can fire out. Penetrating rounds can continue with their remaining energy if the shield breaks. Steel and uranium cannon rounds both take capacity according to their relative impact energy. Boarding craft pass through.

White is regular capacity and red is emergency capacity. A full generator has 750 of each. Regular capacity starts recovering three seconds after regular expenditure, at six points per second while powered. Emergency hits leave that timer alone. Regular recovery can continue during emergency use and in line-shield modes. With the range's 10% automatic rejoin threshold, an empty generator can return with 75 capacity after about 15.5 seconds of uninterrupted recovery. One silver supplies three points of emergency capacity. Filling 750 costs 250 silver.
Fire secondary group 4 and watch how much armour the railgun penetrates after breaking the single shield. Rapid fire can spend capacity frequently, sustained laser fire delays regular recovery, and the railgun makes an effective opening shield breaker. Heavy cannons work better against exposed armour.
LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Guard:
All three guard generators cooperate and start with 2,250 shared regular capacity. The fixed rail lane meets only the northern dome. A hit there draws regular capacity from the two southern generators as well. Once the shared pool is empty, the hit can only spend the northern generator's 750 emergency capacity.

Start with all three generators full. Fire secondary group 4 at full power, then pause as soon as the shot lands and inspect each generator. All three show zero regular capacity. The northern emergency reserve is empty, and each southern reserve still has 750. The shot spends 3,000 capacity at the northern dome and carries its remaining energy into the armour. Compare with the 1,500 capacity of a full single guard. Switching terminal settings preserves existing damage and capacity spent.
Regular recovery has the same three-second wait and restores six points per second per powered emitter, for up to 18 per second together. Emergency hits leave the regular recovery clock running.

LanguageData.DeltaV_Range_Lesson_Introduction:
Welcome to the Starbound Frontier range. Acknowledge these instructions to unlock the blast door.

CONTROLS
Select the platform in the ship control panel on your PDA, arm it and choose manual fire control. The platform starts with fire control disabled. Automatic fire control leaves the allied target alone.
The northern row is the main set (left mouse by default) and the southern row is the secondary set (right mouse). Groups 1, 2 and 3 in each set are rapid cannon, heavy cannon and laser. Main cannons use high-explosive steel. Secondary cannons use armour-piercing uranium. Each cannon starts with both its built-in and auxiliary magazines full of its assigned heads and propellant. Enable one group at a time. Aim due east at the same height as the selected barrel. The railgun at the east end is secondary group 4 and fires along its fixed barrel when triggered.
Both rapid cannons fire every 10 ticks and use four propellant units and ten heads per shot. Both heavy cannons use 48 propellant units and 48 heads. Both lasers use power 3. The range turrets have advanced auto-aim so they can operate without gunners.

SAFETY AND TEST ORDER
The turrets cover an eastward 90-degree sector and have a configured range of 150 cells. Keep other ships clear of the firing lane. Damaging or dismantling allied equipment costs goodwill.
From west to east the columns are unshielded, kinetic, electromagnetic and guard. Start with bare armour, then compare line-shield angles and strengths. Finish by comparing single and joint guard with the railgun. The kinetic and electromagnetic columns each have four terminals in north-to-south order. The third kinetic terminal, 45 degrees at 35%, compares steel and uranium rounds. The target's painted west wall helps you find impacts. The fixed rail lane clears the generators and crosses the armour and isolated empty batteries. The platform carries an experimental 36,000 Wd battery bank.
Shots use real ammunition and energy, and the target takes real damage. Switching terminals preserves previous damage and expenditure.
Our testers joke: “If only this were a game with saves. We could save before testing and reload if we wrecked the target.” I am certainly not hinting at anything. You can head to the station without firing.
